title: Real-valued conversion preserves computation
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be any subset of the $n$ coordinates, let $f$ map the sign cube of dimension $n$ to the two signs, and let $T$ be a finite decision tree with sign-valued queries and outputs whose available coordinates are in $A$. If $T$ computes $f$, then the corresponding binary decision tree computes the real-valued function obtained by converting each binary input coordinate to its sign and interpreting the output sign of $f$ as a real number.
hypotheses_covered: A coordinate subset A of the n coordinates
A function from the n-dimensional sign cube to the two signs
A finite decision tree with sign-valued queries and outputs and available coordinates A
The tree computes the target function
